All five edits improve the text. I lowered the GPS change from 2 to 1: the baseline's «orientarnos más a menudo» was only mildly odd, it partly inherits the slightly odd English 'navigate more often', and «desplazarnos» trades some wayfinding sense for the travel sense. The only remaining items are optional idiom polish. The source's factual doubts are listed separately."},"changeVotes":[{"index":0,"agreeWording":true,"agreeSeverity":false,"severity":1,"rationale":"«Desplazarnos por cualquier ciudad» reads better than «orientarnos más a menudo», and «esquivando» is fine. But the baseline was understandable, and part of the awkwardness comes from the English 'navigate more often' itself. «Desplazarnos» also slightly shifts 'navigate' from wayfinding to travel. That makes it polish, not a noticeable defect."},{"index":1,"agreeWording":true,"agreeSeverity":true,"severity":1,"rationale":"'Improve the environmental impact' clearly means reducing harm, so «reducir» makes the intent explicit without changing the claim. Severity 1 is right because «mejorar el impacto» was understandable and mirrors the loose English."},{"index":2,"agreeWording":true,"agreeSeverity":true,"severity":1,"rationale":"The source has no counterpart for «de los estudiantes»; removing it fixes the repetition and restores fidelity. «Amplifica» is the source's verb and removes the potencia/potenciado echo. Rejecting «su desarrollo» for ambiguity is sound."},{"index":3,"agreeWording":true,"agreeSeverity":true,"severity":1,"rationale":"Spanish orthography requires the closing raya even when a period follows. «Si le queda batería» is the idiomatic way to say 'assuming it has a charge'."},{"index":4,"agreeWording":true,"agreeSeverity":true,"severity":1,"rationale":"«Idiocia» has a clinical/archaic medical ring. «Idiotez» fits the sarcastic register without making it harsher."}],"sourceConcerns":["The source says educators warned about CliffsNotes in the 1940s, but CliffsNotes is commonly dated to 1958. The author should verify this. The translation correctly keeps «década de 1940».","The quote 'crutches that will hobble a generation' is unattributed. The author should confirm it is a real historical quotation and not a paraphrase presented as one.","The claim that most people under 40 can't read paper maps is stated without support. It is kept unchanged in the translation.","The footnote's 'improve the environmental impact' is loose English for reducing harm. The author may want to reword the source."]}
